title: Artichokes and Peas in Garlic Butter (Kharshuf Matbukh)
steps: Trim the artichokes down to their hearts and cut each heart into 4–6 pieces.
prep
Parboil the peas, add the artichokes and boil together until both are tender, then drain.
Crush the garlic with salt and work it into the butter until smooth.
Warm the garlic butter over a very low heat until the garlic turns pale yellow.
Add the vegetables and simmer for about 10 minutes, tossing often.
finish

title: Tunisian Stuffed Artichoke Hearts (Gannariya Mihshiya)
steps: Sauce: fry half the garlic in hot fat, stirring so it does not stick, then add the tomato paste, paprika, salt and pepper thinned with 2 cups of water and simmer for 5 minutes.
prep

Filling: put the beef in a pot with half a cup of water over a high heat and stir until the water has evaporated. Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the parsley, the rest of the garlic, the tabil, salt and pepper and cook for 3 minutes more. Leave to cool.
Boil and mash the potato. Beat the eggs and mix them thoroughly into the meat with the potato.
Fill the artichoke hearts with the meat mixture and arrange them neatly in a pot.
Pour the tomato sauce over them and cook gently until the artichokes are tender.
Add the lemon juice before serving.
finish
notes: A Tunisian dish. The lemon juice appears in the book’s ingredient list without a step; adding it at the end is our suggestion.

title: Black-Eyed Beans and Beef in Tomato (Lubya Nashfa bi-l-Dim‘a)
ingredients: Garlic cloves, peeled and halved diagonally
steps: Soak the beans overnight, drain, then parboil them in fresh water for 5–7 minutes and drain again.
prep
Cut the meat into small cubes and chop the onions.
prep
Soften the onions in the oil, add the meat and fry until the juices it releases have been absorbed again.
Add the beans, parsley, chard, tomato juice, garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook over a low heat until the meat and beans are both tender.
finish

title: White Beans Stewed with Beef and Garlic (Fasulya Beida Matbukha)
ingredients: Garlic cloves, peeled and halved diagonally
steps: Soak the beans overnight, rinse them and boil for 15–30 minutes, until tender, skimming as needed. Drain and set aside.
prep
Cut the meat into bite-sized pieces.
prep
Fry the onions until golden brown, add the meat and fry until it has reabsorbed its juices.
Add the garlic, salt, pepper and just enough water to cover, and cook for about 20 minutes.
Add the beans and simmer for 10 minutes more.
finish
In tomato sauce (recipe 87 in the book): fry the cubed meat until it reabsorbs its juices, simmer it in 2 cups of tomato sauce for 20 minutes, then add the boiled beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
alternative

title: Turkish White Bean Stew (Fasulye Pilaki)
ingredients: Celery stalks and leaves, very finely sliced
steps: Soak the beans for at least 2 hours. Drain, cover with plenty of fresh water, boil for 3–5 minutes, then take off the heat and leave for 1–2 hours.
prep
Fry the onions in olive oil until soft, add the garlic, carrots and celery and fry for 3–5 minutes, stirring.
Bring the beans back to the boil and cook for 30 minutes.
Thin the tomato paste with water, add the sugar, salt and pepper, and add it to the beans with the fried vegetables. Cook until everything is tender.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice, parsley and chili if using, and check the seasoning. Serve hot or cold.
finish

title: Kibbeh in Yogurt with Chickpeas (Kubeiba Labaniya)
ingredients: Kibbeh paste (fine bulgur, beef, fat and onion)
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight, drain, and parboil in fresh water for 5–7 minutes. Drain.
prep
Make kibbeh paste as for the fried kubeiba discs in this collection (bulgur soaked for an hour, then minced repeatedly with beef, fat and onion into a soft dough).
prep
Either shape it into hollow balls filled with spiced minced beef and pine nuts, or cut it into thin discs. Do not fry them.
Put the kibbeh in a pot with the chickpeas.
Stir the egg white into the yogurt to stop it curdling and press it through a sieve over the kibbeh.
Cook uncovered for 60–90 minutes.
Sprinkle with the mint and serve hot or cold.
finish
notes: Made in Lebanon, Syria and Palestine.

title: Cauliflower Stewed with Beef and Tomato (‘Arnabit Matbukh)
steps: Break the cauliflower into florets and cut the meat into bite-sized pieces. Peel and dice the tomatoes and chop the onions very finely.
prep
Fry the onions in the oil until pale yellow, add the tomatoes and cook for 7–10 minutes.
Add the meat with salt and pepper and cook for about 20 minutes.
Add the cauliflower and simmer for about 10 minutes, until tender.
finish

With garlic instead of tomato (recipe 106 in the book): fry the onions, brown the meat until it reabsorbs its juices, cover with water, add 7–10 halved garlic cloves with the seasoning and cook for 20 minutes, then add the cauliflower for 10 minutes.
alternative

title: Baked Chicken with Tomatoes and Onions (Tagin Firakh)
steps: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces.
prep
Mix the spice with salt and pepper and rub it lightly over the chicken.
Lay the pieces in a lightly greased roasting pan and cover them with the seasoned onions and tomatoes.
Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 60–90 minutes, basting with the pan juices.
Thicken the juices with cornflour if you like.
finish

With carrots and celery (recipe 110 in the book): brown chopped onions and celery in oil, cover the chicken with them and with parboiled carrot rounds and halved garlic cloves, pour meat stock over and bake the same way.
alternative

title: Chicken in Mastic Milk Sauce (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Laban)
steps: Cut each chicken into 6–8 pieces.
prep
Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover at once and turn off the heat. Leave for 1–2 minutes so the chicken takes on the scent.
Turn the heat back on and brown the chicken, then lift it out.
Fry the flour in the same oil until light brown. Off the heat, whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth.
Return to the heat, season, and when it bubbles add the chicken.
Cook uncovered for about 20 minutes, until tender.
finish

title: Chicken with Green Olives (Firakh bi-l-Zatun al-Akhdar)
steps: Cut each chicken into 4–6 pieces. Boil the olives in fresh water for 1 minute, drain, pit and halve them.
prep
Heat the oil, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chicken, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry the chicken until browned and lift it out.
Soften the onion in the same oil and set it aside with the chicken.
Fry the flour until golden. Off the heat, whisk in 1 cup of warm water a little at a time.
Return to the heat and, when the gravy bubbles, add the chicken, onion, salt and pepper. Cook over a very low heat for about 20 minutes.
Add the olives and lemon juice and simmer for 2–3 minutes more.
finish

title: Giblet-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mihammara)
ingredients: Chickens, about 1 kg each, with giblets
Onions (2 for the stuffing, 1 for the broth)
steps: Finely chop two onions and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Mix them with the spice, salt and pepper.
prep
Stuff the chickens with the mixture and sew them up.
prep
Bring enough water to half-cover the chickens to the boil with the remaining onion and salt, add the chickens and cook for about 20 minutes, then lift them out.
Heat oil in another pot, stir in the mastic for 10 seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes.
Fry the chickens, turning them until browned all over.
finish

title: Giblet-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Firakh Mahshiya wi Mashwiya)
ingredients: Chickens, about 1 kg each, with giblets
steps: Chop the onions very finely and cut the gizzards and hearts into very small pieces. Season, add the spice and mix.
prep
Stuff the chickens and sew them up.
prep
Mix the tomato paste, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper and rub it all over the chickens.
Roast in a hot oven, basting two or three times with the juices.
finish

title: Lebanese Lemon Chicken with Olives (Djaj bi Leimoon Hamed)
steps: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in oil; set aside.
prep
Put the onions, garlic, coriander and parsley in a pot, add the saffron and leave over a very low heat until soft.
Add the chicken with its oil, salt, pepper and 1 cup of hot water. Cover and cook slowly, stirring now and then.
When the chicken is done, move it to a platter. Mash the vegetables well, add the lemon juice and olives and let it bubble for 2–3 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the chicken and serve.
finish

title: Chicken in Pomegranate and Walnut Sauce (Fesenjan)
steps: Cut the chickens into neat joints, fry them lightly on all sides and keep them warm.
prep
Soften the onions in the same oil.
Add the walnuts, broth, sugar, pomegranate juice, salt and pepper and cook until the sauce thickens.
Return the chicken and cook over a low heat for 20–25 minutes more.
finish
notes: An Iranian dish; the book spells it Faisinjan.

title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Chicken, Boiled then Fried (Djaj Mihshy)
ingredients: Chickens, about 1 kg each, with giblets
steps: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
prep
Bring 4 cups of water to the boil with the onion and seasoning, add the chickens and cook for 20–30 minutes. Lift them out and keep warm.
Heat oil, stir in the mastic for a few seconds, add the chickens, cover tightly and turn off the heat for 2–3 minutes.
Uncover and fry the chickens until nicely browned.
Cut them into joints, heap the stuffing in the middle of a dish and arrange the chicken around it. Moisten the stuffing with a little warm broth if you like.
finish

title: Lebanese Rice-Stuffed Roast Chicken (Djaj Mihshy)
ingredients: Chickens, about 1 kg each, with giblets
steps: Dice the giblets and mix them with the rice, spice, salt and pepper. Stuff the chickens and truss or sew them closed.
prep
Thin the tomato paste with the lemon juice, add salt, pepper and the oil, and rub the mixture over the chickens inside and out.
Roast, basting often with the lemon mixture.
finish

title: Chicken Simmered in Yogurt with Mint (Firakh Matbukha bi-l-Zabadi)
steps: Cut the chickens into neat joints and fry them lightly in olive oil.
prep
Stir the egg white into the yogurt to keep it from splitting and press it through a sieve over the chicken.
Season and cook uncovered for about 30 minutes.
Thicken with the cornflour, move to a serving dish and sprinkle with the mint.
finish

title: Sumac-Onion Chicken Baked in Bread (Frakh Mashwiya bi-l-Summa’)
steps: Grate the onions and mix with the sumac, salt, pepper and olive oil.
prep
Rub the chickens with the mixture and push the rest inside them.
Wrap each chicken in a loaf of bread, then in foil.
Cook slowly in the middle of a low, preheated oven until the chicken is tender.
finish
notes: A Palestinian dish related to musakhan. The book gives no time; allow about 1 1/2 hours in a low oven.

title: Tunisian Fish Couscous with Fish Balls (Couscous bil Hout)
ingredients: Marinade: fennel seeds and caraway seeds
Fish balls: grated onion, 3–5 crushed garlic cloves, 1 egg and half a stale loaf
Fish balls: chopped parsley, a dash of harissa and paprika
Onions, zucchini, carrots, artichoke hearts and tomatoes
Cloves, a piece of cinnamon bark and caraway seeds
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then boil them in fresh water until tender. Drain, keeping the liquid.
prep
Mix the marinade ingredients and leave the fish fillets in it for 1–2 hours.
prep

Fish balls: moisten the bread with water. Steam and flake the whiting and mix it with a purée of the onion and garlic, the paprika, harissa, parsley, beaten egg, bread, salt and pepper. Roll into small balls, fry until brown and keep warm.
prep

Vegetables: brown the grated onions in oil, then stir in the sliced zucchini and carrots, chopped artichokes and diced tomatoes until coated with oil. Add the spices tied in muslin, the chickpeas and enough of their liquid to cover, and cook over a low heat.

Sprinkle the couscous with cold water and steam it in a perforated steamer set over the vegetable pot, covered. Once or twice, uncover, sprinkle with a little cold water and fluff the grains with a fork so they do not form lumps. Keep steaming until the vegetables are tender.
Brush the marinade off the fish and grill the fillets on both sides.
Pile the couscous in a serving bowl, top with the grilled fish and fish balls, and serve the vegetables separately.
finish

title: Tunisian Couscous with Mutton and Dates (Couscous bi Tamr)
steps: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Peel and dice the carrots and turnips.
prep
Boil the meat and vegetables in salted water.
When the meat is nearly done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the pot for 5–7 minutes.
Uncover, sprinkle lightly with water and break up any lumps with a fork.
Stone and roughly chop the dates, mix them into the couscous and return it to steam over the meat until both are fully cooked. Keep them separate.
Pour a ladle of the meat broth over the garlic, harissa and chili and boil hard until reduced by half.
Serve the couscous, the meat and the sauce separately.
finish

title: Lebanese Chicken Maghrabiyeh
steps: Cut the chicken into neat joints.
prep
Bring water to the boil with the onions, mastic, salt and pepper, add the chicken and cook.
About 10–15 minutes before the chicken is done, sprinkle the couscous with water and steam it over the broth, uncovering once or twice to break up lumps with a fork and sprinkle with more cold water.
When the couscous is tender, move it to a deep bowl and keep warm.
Lift out the chicken and fry the joints in oil.
Mash the onion into the broth, thicken it, check the seasoning and serve it separately as a sauce.
finish

title: Fried Eggplant Baked in Tahini (Bitingan Ma’li bi-l-Tahina)
steps: Slice the eggplants lengthwise about 2 cm thick, sprinkle with salt and leave for at least an hour. Squeeze gently, drain and pat dry.
prep
Deep-fry the slices until dark brown and drain on absorbent paper.
Make a thin tahini sauce: whisk the tahini with the water, lemon juice, vinegar, cumin, salt and garlic until smooth.
Arrange the eggplant in a baking pan and pour the tahini sauce over.
Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.
finish

title: Mashed Fried Eggplant with Garlic Yogurt (Beitinjan Mifassakh)
steps: Slice and salt the eggplants for an hour, then squeeze and pat dry.
prep
Fry them in olive oil until soft and brown.
Mash with the yogurt and garlic.
Stir in the parsley and serve.
finish

title: Turkish Eggplant Cream (Hünkar Beğendi)
steps: Roast the eggplants whole in their skins, in a hot oven or on a tray over the stove, turning them when one side softens. Peel, drain and mash the flesh.
prep
Melt the butter and cook the flour in it over a very low heat until golden.
Off the heat, stir in the hot milk, then return to the heat and let it bubble.
Stir in the eggplant, season and cook for 10 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cheese and parsley and serve.
finish
notes: A Turkish dish, usually served under braised meat.

title: Imam Bayildi with Minced Beef and Yogurt
ingredients: Pine nuts, pecans or hazelnuts, chopped
steps: Slice, salt and drain the eggplants, then deep-fry them until dark brown.
prep
Brown the onion in a little oil, add the beef with salt and pepper and cook until its juices are absorbed.
prep
Put the meat and fried eggplant in a pot over a low heat and cook, stirring often, until the eggplant has completely broken down.
Press the mixture against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon to squeeze out excess fat, and pour it off.
Spread in a shallow dish. Mix the yogurt with the garlic and a little salt and spread it over the top.
Sprinkle with the nuts and serve hot or cold.
finish
notes: “Imam bayildi” is Turkish for “the imam fainted”: legend says the imam swooned with delight at the smell of the dish. The book gives four different recipes under this name, with eggplant as the only common ingredient; this is its first and second (they differ only in how the yogurt is seasoned), and the other two follow.

title: Imam Bayildi: Rice-Stuffed Eggplants in Olive Oil
steps: Core the eggplants and drop them straight into salted water so they do not darken.
prep
Mix all the stuffing ingredients together.
prep
Fill the eggplants loosely, leaving room for the rice to swell, and pack them neatly in a pot.
Dissolve the tomato paste and sugar in enough water to cover the eggplants, add the olive oil and lemon juice, and pour over.
Bring to the boil over a high heat, then lower the heat and simmer until the eggplants are very tender.
Serve hot or cold.
finish
notes: The third of the book’s four imam bayildi recipes.

title: Imam Bayildi: Baked Eggplant Shells with Currants
steps: Soak the currants in lukewarm water.
prep
Halve the eggplants lengthwise and scoop out the flesh without piercing the skins. Dice or mash the flesh and sprinkle it with lemon juice.
prep
Fry the eggplant flesh with the onions in the oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Cover and cook over a low heat for about 20 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the garlic and the drained currants.
Arrange the eggplant shells in a well-greased baking dish and fill them with the mixture.
Drizzle a little olive oil over each and bake in a slow oven until the shells are soft.
finish
notes: The fourth of the book’s imam bayildi recipes.

title: Poached Fish Sayadiya with Brown Onion Rice (Sayadiyit al-Samak)
steps: Fry the onion in the oil until deep brown.
Add about 2 cups of water with salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
Add the fish and poach over a low heat for 10 minutes.
Strain the broth, top it up with water and use it to cook the rice (fry the rice briefly in a little oil first, then simmer until the liquid is absorbed).
Skin, bone and flake the fish and fold it through the rice.
finish

title: Fried Fish Sayadiya (Sayadiyit Samak Ma’li)
steps: Cut the fish into neat pieces, fry them and drain on absorbent paper.
prep
Fry the onion in the same oil until deep brown.
Add the rice and water with salt and cook uncovered until the water has been absorbed.
Lay the fried fish on top of the rice, turn the heat to its lowest, cover and cook for 15–20 minutes.
Serve the fish on its rice.
finish

title: Fish and Vegetables Baked in Tahini (Samak bi-l-Khudar wi-l-Tahina)
ingredients: Sweet peppers, seeded and thinly sliced
Tahini sauce (tahini thinned with water, lemon, vinegar, cumin and salt)
steps: Cut the fish into large chunks, coat them in seasoned flour and fry. Drain, cool and flake.
prep
Parboil the carrots and slice them thinly.
prep
Sauté the onions and sweet peppers and mix them into the fish with the carrots and eggs.
Spread the mixture in a baking pan and cover it with the tahini sauce.
Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 15 minutes.
finish
